generation.final_prompt:
Rendering style:
Create an authored editorial illustration for a serious technology newspaper.

Direction:
- authored editorial print language
- deliberate simplified shapes with clear focal hierarchy
- restrained limited palette
- subtle physical print texture
- controlled abstraction and strong negative space
- non-photorealistic but factually grounded representation
- newspaper and social-card readability

Fixed factual and safety restrictions:
- Do not render visible text, captions, headlines, or newspaper typography.
- Do not render logos or trademarks.
- Do not fabricate visible factual evidence.
- Do not render interfaces or screenshots.
- Do not imitate a named or living artist.

Profile-specific exclusions:
- glossy CGI
- luxury product render
- generic futuristic concept art
- cyberpunk or neon
- glowing circuit-board decoration
- floating particles
- heroic centered hardware
- server rack treated as monument or skyscraper
- generic server room
- advertising composition
- airbrushed gradients
- synthetic chrome
- excessive pseudo-technical detail
- malformed or visible text
- labels
- diagrams with words

Exact source facts:
Title: AGENTIC OFFENSIVE FRAMEWORKS HIT REAL INTRUSIONS
Summary: Google Threat Intelligence Group (GTIG) and Mandiant observed intruders using the open-source ARTEX framework with stolen credentials and letting its six sub-agents run Azure and AWS permission sweeps, Kerberoasting, DCSync, and MySQL log poisoning that wrote JSP webshells in bursts as short as 2 to 25 seconds. ARTEX users included financially motivated extortion groups and suspected PRC-nexus clusters such as UNC7228, which went from a first account to deep access in about four hours, though GTIG noted the agents were forensically noisy and sometimes undid each other's work. Mandiant recommended short-lived, tightly scoped credentials, locking down admin interfaces like Kudu/SCM as privileged infrastructure, and behavioral detection tuned for machine-speed bursts.

Editorial idea:
Machine-speed intrusion changes the tempo of cloud attacks faster than defenders can respond.

Central subject:
An intrusion in which ARTEX sub-agents rapidly expand access across Azure and AWS environments.

Visual relationship:
Automated offensive activity moves through privileged systems in seconds while human defenders must detect, verify, and contain it.

Composition:
A branching sequence of access points and compromised services advances in tightly compressed bursts from one initial credential, while a slower defensive inspection line attempts to trace and stop the spread; show activity as grounded system connections rather than decorative symbols.

Permitted literal elements:
A stolen credential as the starting access point
Azure and AWS permission paths
Multiple concurrent sub-agent activity trails
Short bursts representing two-to-25-second operations
A separate slower defensive review path

Abstraction level:
medium

Story-specific forbidden elements:
Decorative server racks
Generic computers or laptops
Robots
Cloud icons
Shields
Arrows without factual system relationships
Charts
Logos
Rendered text

Likely failure modes to avoid:
Portraying the agents as autonomous humanoid attackers
Suggesting the intrusion was silent or perfectly coordinated when the source notes forensic noise
Showing unsupported physical data-center details
Reducing the story to a generic cybersecurity lock-and-key image

Global factual restrictions:
Do not fabricate visible factual evidence. Do not imitate a named or living artist. Do not render interfaces or screenshots.
Do not render any words, letters, numbers, labels, captions, annotations, signage, diagrams with text, logos, watermarks, or pseudo-writing anywhere in the image.
If the concept cannot be represented without visible text, represent the relationship through shape, scale, spacing, direction, grouping, interruption, containment, or contrast instead.
